Mickey Thomas Reflects on Decades with Starship, Hits, and Musical Evolution

The Voice Behind the 1980s Hits

For more than four decades, vocalist Mickey Thomas has remained a prominent voice in classic rock, best known for fronting Starship through their peak commercial era in the 1980s. In a detailed retrospective interview with Rolling Stone, Thomas reflected on his extensive career, which spans the gradual evolution of Jefferson Airplane into Jefferson Starship and eventually the pop powerhouse Starship.

While classic rock fans frequently associate the band with its 1960s psychedelic roots under Jefferson Airplane, Thomas fronted the lineup responsible for major 1980s chart-toppers including 'We Built This City,' 'Sara,' and 'Nothing’s Gonna Stop Us Now.' He also famously sang lead on Elvin Bishop’s 1976 smash hit, 'Fooled Around and Fell in Love,' a track that served as a major stepping stone in his professional trajectory.

Navigating Band Changes and Critical Backlash

Thomas joined the evolving lineup in 1979 at the invitation of founding member Paul Kantner, making his debut on the album Freedom at Point Zero and lending his vocals to the rock staple 'Jane.' The transition required taking the stage without original vocalists Grace Slick and Marty Balin, a challenge that demanded rebuilding the audience from the ground up before Slick eventually returned to the fold.

Looking back at the shifting musical landscape of the 1980s, Thomas addressed the retrospective criticism surrounding tracks like 'We Built This City,' which was infamously labeled by Blender magazine in 2004 as one of the worst songs of all time. Thomas noted that the negative perception developed years later as a reaction to the broader industry shift from analog recording to the digital era.

Practical Implications and What Readers Can Verify

  • Live Performances: Mickey Thomas currently tours and performs classic material under the banner of Starship Featuring Mickey Thomas, playing a setlist that includes both 1980s Starship hits and earlier Jefferson Airplane and Jefferson Starship catalog tracks.
  • Touring Entities: A separate touring entity, Jefferson Starship, also features veteran members from the band's extensive history.
